required_secrets.note: The combined `github` envelope (github_core >= v0.5.0, req-github-core-app-auth): an `app` block — a READ-ONLY GitHub App installed on the observed account (`data.owner`), minted with github_core's create-github-app skill — and/or a `pat` block — a fine-grained READ-ONLY PAT whose resource owner is the observed account, minted by hand in GitHub's UI — routed per collection source, never by preference order. Legacy `github_pat` / `github_app` envelopes still fold on read. Permissions are the union of what github_core's collection manifest declares per source; its App-permission ledger (github_app_permissions.json) is the authoritative list, and packages stay unobservable under an App credential until GitHub enables that surface for Apps.

description: git-serious double-tap — the unified-systems-com INSTANCE composition: git-serious (the product, plan/product-map.md) plus the double-tap plugin that holds only what is specific to observing the organization that builds TAP. Installs the product's closure exactly as git-serious's own record does (git_core first, then identity_core, github_core, administrivia at the same pins; git_serious from its repo), then the instance plugin; seeds the product's pages, then the instance's; fires the github_core collector against unified-systems-com. The landing page is decided HERE, by the operator, per req-web-page-landing: web pins the /double-tap page by entity id with its slug as a verified assertion — git-serious alone lands on /git-serious, this composition lands on /double-tap. DEV-PHASE record: git_serious and git_serious_double_tap pin branches until each has a tagged release (req-boot-bootstrap-stage0-3); the first tagged release replaces them and drops the marker.

steps.note: ONLY the workflow page (/github_core/workflow), which every workflow node on this instance's machinery graphs navigates to; without this step github_core is installed but never populated and every such click 404s (git-serious-double-tap#31). The repo-landing bundle stays out on purpose: it seeds /samsite/repo, and git-serious owns the repository page. Before git_serious: a later bundle's edge into this page must find it, and the importer only warns on a dangling endpoint.
git-serious landing page: the account's CI/CD system as a graph.

zizmor's own bundles: the /zizmor landing page (about, findings, coverage, runs) and the schedule that re-audits on its own cadence. Owned by the plugin rather than by this instance because the finding set is a property of the scanner and its pin, not of this instance's pages.
The instance's pages. MUST follow git_serious's seed: its USES_PANEL edges target panels git_serious seeds, and the importer only warns on a dangling endpoint.

Pulls the configured scope onto the grid: the account's repositories, workflows, runs, jobs, runners, apps. Fires against whatever github_pat envelope is placed — until the account-scoped PAT lands this is the shared repos-only credential, which makes the first boot an end-to-end smoke test of the collector path rather than the org picture.

MUST stay after github_core:github_core. Its input is the workflow YAML that step lands, and the collector refuses to produce findings it cannot attribute to a completed github_core collection. It also guards its own freshness: a fire that finds a github_core collection still in flight finalizes as skipped and creates no run node rather than auditing rows mid-write, so reordering these two makes zizmor silently produce nothing. No secrets: the run is offline and credential-free.

fips_waivers.reason: zizmor's wheel is one static Rust binary that links boringssl (via ring) and aws-lc-rs for an HTTPS client used only by its ONLINE audits. This plugin invokes it with --offline and hands it an environment carrying no GitHub token, so the providers are present in the artifact but never execute a security operation. No TAP data is encrypted, signed or hashed by them. Re-decide when req-zizmor-online-audits ships: that turns the providers from present-but-unreached into actually executing. (Scoped by `artifact` rather than `plugin`: tap.crypto_bom.load_waivers resolves `entry.get('artifact') or entry.get('plugin')`, so supplying both would silently drop the plugin key — a field that reads as if it narrows the waiver and does not.)

The second non-validated provider in the same static binary, waived on the same basis and with the same re-decision trigger. AWS-LC has a FIPS 140-3 validated module, but it ships as a separate crate (aws-lc-fips-sys) that zizmor's build does not select, so the binary is not the validated module even though the library it embeds is validatable. (Scoped by `artifact` rather than `plugin`: tap.crypto_bom.load_waivers resolves `entry.get('artifact') or entry.get('plugin')`, so supplying both would silently drop the plugin key — a field that reads as if it narrows the waiver and does not.)
